title: Do Sanctions Backfire? New Evidence on the Macroeconomic Effects of Supporting Ukraine (Vicente Rios, Izaskun Barba, Lisa Gianmoena, September 11 2026)
hypothesis: Main boomerang effect operates through prices rather than output: relative to 2019-2021, significant post-2022 increase in log CPI among sanctioning countries (0.072 log points ~7.5%, ***), robust across counterfactuals, reference windows, inference; no robust evidence of aggregate GDP-per-capita losses (incremental 0.025*** preferred but reference-dependent, placebo 0.102, factor-sensitive). Cross-country heterogeneity linked to pre-war Russian fossil-energy imports/GDP: +1 SD 2018-2021 exposure associated +2.2pp CPI differential (~0.0213) and -0.96pp annual GDPpc growth differential within coalition.
data_sources: WDI (FP.CPI.TOTL, NY.GDP.PCAP.KD, FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, NY.GDP.PCAP.KD.ZG, NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS, NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS, TT.PRI.MRCH.XD.WD, NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, NE.CON.GOVT.ZS, SP.POP.GROW, TM.VAL.FUEL.ZS.UN, TX.VAL.FUEL.ZS.UN), WGI rule of law, Council Regulation (EU) No.833/2014 and Council/European Commission records, dated Council alignment declarations, Switzerland ordinance 2 April 2014, New Zealand Russia Sanctions Act 2022, March 2022 Singapore/South Korea announcements, cross-checked with Ukraine Support Tracker Kiel and Global Sanctions Data Base Release 4, UN Comtrade HS coal/crude/refined/LNG/gas imports from Russia and world totals. Appendix Tables A1, A4, A5, A8 detail sources.
sample: Balanced annual panel. Countries from available World Bank country database universe retained only if raw outcome and control coverage satisfies thresholds without using policy indicators: (i) none of 4 outcomes >35% raw missing over 2000-2024; (ii) at most one of 8 controls >25% raw missing; (iii) no control >65% raw missing; (iv) CPI and real GDP per capita each no more than 25% raw missing during 2019-2024. Starting 131 otherwise eligible countries, critical-window screen excludes Syria and Sudan. Final N=129 countries. Panel observed 2000-2024, effective estimation 2001-2024 after 1-year lag of controls, untreated-model estimation 2001-2013. Country-years 3,225 (129*25). 1996-1999 used only as supporting observations for completion, not counted. Treatment status, estimated effects and imputed values do not determine eligibility. Raw outcome missing: Real GDP per capita 0, GDP-per-capita growth 0, CPI 25 (0.78%), inflation 32 (0.99%); total 57 of 12,900 outcome cells 0.44% (55 leading 2000-2007 bounded local-trend backcasts, 2 Bosnia and Herzegovina 2024 carried forward from 2023). Controls raw missing 1,471 of 25,800 control cells 5.70% completed via deterministic hierarchy: internal gap linear interpolation, trailing gap last observation, leading gap <=3 years first observation, longer leading gap local linear trend from first 5 valid observations bounded by country historical range +/-1 SD, non-negative constraint for trade openness, investment, government consumption. Russia, Belarus, Ukraine excluded from every donor pool by geopolitical design. Ukraine remains sanctions-coded in descriptive N=129 but excluded from main sanctions ATT. Donor eligibility determined separately per policy-outcome. Exposure analysis uses separate UN Comtrade construction universe for same 129 countries, windows 2010-2013 and 2018-2021 (1,032 potential country-year cells); Russia, Belarus, Ukraine not in 126-country mechanism universe; nominal GDP positive in all cells; pipeline-gas unresolved for Austria, Germany, Poland, Turkiye excluded under strict and extended rules.
method: Step 1 - Sample construction. Start World Bank country database universe. Apply eligibility thresholds above on raw 2000-2024 data before any completion. Exclude Syria and Sudan under 2019-2024 25% rule (Sudan 2 raw missing CPI in 2019-2024, Syria 5 raw missing CPI and 2 raw missing real GDP per capita). Retain N=129. Observed years 2000-2024, effective estimation years 2001-2024 after lagging controls, untreated-model estimation window P={2001,...,2013} T0=13.

Step 2 - Variables and transformations. Outcomes: log CPI (FP.CPI.TOTL log after completion, within-country index), log real GDP per capita (NY.GDP.PCAP.KD log), inflation rate (FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG /100), real GDPpc growth (NY.GDP.PCAP.KD.ZG /100). Controls (all lagged 1 year): oil rents NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS, trade openness NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS, terms of trade TT.PRI.MRCH.XD.WD, investment rate NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, government consumption NE.CON.GOVT.ZS, rule of law WGI, population growth SP.POP.GROW, fuel-share balance TM.VAL.FUEL.ZS.UN minus TX.VAL.FUEL.ZS.UN. Source Appendix Table A1.

Step 3 - Policy coding. Sanctions indicator S_it =1 from first calendar year legally covered by official sanctions regime against Russia or formal alignment; EU members 2014, others dated national measure. 43 sanctions-coded, 42 main sanctions targets (Ukraine excluded from ATT). Direct-arming indicator =1 from first year publicly verifiable lethal weapons delivery/commitment; broad non-lethal, purely financial, indirect, leaked, insufficiently documented not coded. 29 direct-arming (28 both policies +1 direct-only). Descriptive categories: sanctions only 14, direct-only 1, neither 83, both 28, geopolitical exclusions 3 (Russia, Belarus, Ukraine). Donor pools: sanctions log CPI 84, log GDPpc 84 (86 candidates minus BLR,RUS); direct-arming log CPI 96 (100 candidates minus BIH,BLR,RUS,UKR; BIH excluded for CPI because 2024 repaired in 2019-2024 window), log GDPpc 97 (100 minus BLR,RUS,UKR).

Step 4 - Counterfactual model. Potential outcome Y_it(inf) = X_{i,t-1}'beta + alpha_i' f_t + epsilon_it with alpha_i 2-vector, f_t latent common factors; more flexible than common year effects. Proxy fhat_t = [1, Ybar_{t,CY}]' where Ybar_{t,CY}=|CY|^{-1} sum_{j in CY} Y_{jt} using eligible never-treated donors only for each policy-outcome. Preferred parsimonious specification uses only donor mean of outcome being modeled, not CSAs of covariates, to avoid contaminating proxy with coalition post-2013 outcomes and collinearity in T0=13.

Step 5 - Estimation pre-2013. For each policy-outcome, compute donor factor fhat_t for all years. Using t<=2013, OLS Y_it = X_{i,t-1}'beta + alpha_i' fhat_t + u_it. Stack pre-treatment Fhat = [fhat_{2001}' ; ... ; fhat_{2013}'] T0x2. Residual-maker M_{Fhat}=I - Fhat Fhat^+ where ^+ Moore-Penrose (ordinary inverse if full rank). Residualize Y_i, X_i. Pooled beta estimator betahat = (sum_{i in SY} Xtilde_i' Xtilde_i)^+ (sum Xtilde_i' Ytilde_i) with SY target+donor countries; negligible residual variance columns omitted coefficient zero. Country loadings alphahat_i = (Fhat'Fhat)^{-1} Fhat'(Y_i - X_i betahat) (eq 5) and Lambda_i = (Fhat'Fhat)^{-1} Fhat' X_i (eq 6) 2xK per target (2 loadings per covariate).

Step 6 - Post-2013 counterfactual. Do not condition on target realized controls. Simulate untreated covariate path Xhat_{i,t-1}(inf)= Lambda_i' fhat_t for t>=2014, then Yhat_it(inf)= Xhat_{i,t-1}(inf)' betahat + alphahat_i' fhat_t (eq 8). Observed target post-2013 outcomes/covariates not entering own counterfactual. Gap ghat_it = Y_it - Yhat_it(inf).

Step 7 - Aggregation. For reporting window W in {W1={2014,...,2021} (8 years), W2={2022,...,2024} (3 years)} equally-weighted ATT_W = 1/NT sum_{i in T*} (1/|W| sum_{t in W} ghat_it). NT=|T*| 42 sanctions, 29 direct-arming. For incremental Wave2, define baseline bi =1/3 sum_{t=2019}^{2021} ghat_it, continuation Ycont_it = Yhat_it(inf)+bi for t in W2, ATT_Inc,2 =1/NT sum [(1/3 sum_{2022}^{2024} ghat_it - 1/3 sum_{2019}^{2021} ghat_it)] equivalent. Exact percentage 100[exp(theta)-1], approx 100 theta.

Step 8 - Inference baseline. Country-dispersion SE = sd(d_i)/sqrt(NT) where d_i is complete country contrast (window average or incremental). Two-sided p with Student t_{NT-1}, stars *,**,*** for p<0.10,0.05,0.01 determines stars. Annual observations collapsed, treats country contrasts independent, conditions on estimated factor; does not propagate all first-stage uncertainty.

Step 9 - Bootstrap and placebo. Country-history bootstrap B=500: sample NT target IDs and NC donor IDs iid with replacement, each brings whole 2000-2024 history, new synthetic identifiers, multiplicity; donor mean Ybar^{CH,b}=1/NC sum Y_{I^C}, rebuild factor and re-estimate complete design, store tau_b^{CH}=1/NT sum d^{CH,b}. Region-block bootstrap B=500: World Bank regions G, counts T_g, C_g^Y, residual block OTHER, sample G region IDs with replacement, counts N_{T,b}^{RB}=sum a_gb|T_g|, donor mean Ybar^{RB,b}=sum a_gb sum Y_{jt} / N_{C,b}^{RB}, rebuild, require non-empty target/donor, attempt limit 20*B sanctions-CPI 30*B others, unstudentized percentile interval [Q0.025,Q0.975], sd and sign probabilities stored. Size-matched placebo B=500 assignments without replacement: pseudo-target set T_b^P uniform subset of CY size NT, C_b^P=CY\T_b^P, rebuild factor from C_b^P, complete estimate tau_b^P, two-sided finite-draw p = (1+ sum 1{|tau_b^P|>=|tau|})/(B+1), one-sided plus stored; seeds 24680,26680,27680,28680 for bootstraps, 12345 for placebos; sanctions selects 42 pseudo-targets leaving 42 pseudo-donors, direct-arming selects 29 leaving 67 CPI /68 GDPpc psuedo-donors.

Step 10 - Robustness. Alternative references R={2017-2019,2021,2017-2021,2018-2021} hold W2 fixed; active-year averaging only years with strict indicator active; exclude 2024 horizon 2022-2023; rate outcomes inflation and GDPpc growth; donor-pool variants (corrected full, no repaired main-outcome cells, high-income donors); factor-proxy variants (own-outcome, other-outcome, both, own+oil rents, own+fuel-share) report rank 2-3 and condition number 91-4409; comparability: high-income sample restrict at median 2009-2013 GDPpc, Mahalanobis M=5 nearest donors with frequency weights standardized features m_ij=[(Z_i-Z_j)'(Shat+1e-6I)^+ (Z_i-Z_j)]^{1/2}, SD_k=(Q_Tbar - Q_Cbar)/s_{Q,I}, max|std diff| falls 1.498 to 1.175/1.052; influence: treated LOO tau_{(-i)}=1/(NT-1)sum_{k!=i} d_k, donor LOO rebuild factor re-estimate; direct-arming boundary 29 targets.

Step 11 - Exposure heterogeneity. Separate estimator CCE interaction on observed panel without 8 lagged controls: Y_it = mu_i + lambda_i Ybar_{C,t} + beta1 S_i Post_t + beta2 E_iw Post_t + beta3 S_i E_iw Post_t + u_it, Post=1 in 2022-2024 omitted earlier years not 2019-2021 reference, E_iw = sum Russian fossil imports (coal+crude+refined+gas)/sum GDP over window w standardized, windows 2018-2021 near-prewar and 2010-2013 pre-Crimea, Comtrade screened positives/verified zeros/missing, 37 primitive imputations (13 Russian gas,13 world gas,11 non-gas) via log(1+x) interpolation internal gap <=2 years median growth bounded 5th/95th, strict requires >=3/4 usable <=1 imputed per component else extended >=2/4 <=2; exclude AUT,DEU,POL,TUR pipeline undercoverage; regression samples 118 (39 sanc) for 2018-2021 and 119 (39) for 2010-2013 vs construction 120/121; country-clustered SE; beta1 differential at mean, beta2 non-sanctioner slope, beta3 differential slope, beta2+beta3 sanctioner slope.
